UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
FOR THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF VIRGINIA
ALEXANDRIA DIVISION
MARVELLE J. BALLENTINE,
Plaintiff,
Case No. 1:26-cv-02331
V.
KATIE HALL, individually;
NATIONAL CENTER FOR MISSING & EXPLOITED
CHILDREN;
META PLATFORMS, INC.;
and JOHN/JANE DOES 1-6,
Defendants.
PLAINTIFF'S RULE 201 REQUEST FOR JUDICIAL NOTICE
Plaintiff Marvelle J. Ballentine requests under Federal Rule of Evidence 201(c)(2) that the
Court take judicial notice of the existence, filing date, signatories, and text of one court record:
ECF No. 152 in Ballentine v. Meta Platforms, Inc., No. 3:26-cv-05939-RFL (N.D. Cal.). A
complete copy of ECF No. 152 is attached as Exhibit A. A Memorandum in Support accompanies
this Request.
1.
GROUNDS
1.
Federal Rule of Evidence 201(b)(2) permits the Court to notice a fact that "can be
accurately and readily determined from sources whose accuracy cannot reasonably be questioned."
Rule 201(c)(2) provides that the Court "must take judicial notice if a party requests it and the court
is supplied with the necessary information." Rule 201(d) provides that the Court "may take judicial
notice at any stage of the proceeding."
1

Exhibit A is a complete copy of ECF No. 152 as filed in the United States District
Court for the Northern District of California. Each of its 25 pages bears that court's electronic
filing header, including "Case 3:26-cv-05939-RFL Document 152 Filed 08/13/26" and a page
number. Citations to Exhibit A are to the page numbers in that header.
ECF No. 152 is pleaded in the proposed Second Amended and Supplemental
Complaint. ECF No. 59-1 99 164-169. It is described in the memorandum supporting that
pleading. ECF No. 60 at 9. Leave to file that pleading was denied. ECF No. 84 at 2. Plaintiff's
objections and motions concerning that denial are pending. ECF Nos. 89, 90, 93. Plaintiff's motion
for leave to amend, filed separately, attaches a Proposed Second Amended Complaint that also
pleads ECF No. 152. Proposed Second Am. Compl. 91 180-185.
II.
FACTS TO BE NOTICED
4.
Plaintiff requests notice of the following five facts, and no others.
(a)
Existence and date. A document was filed on August 13, 2026 in Ballentine v.
Meta Platforms, Inc., No. 3:26-cv-05939-RFL (N.D. Cal.), and docketed as ECF No. 152. Ex. A
at 1-25 (header).
(b)
Title. ECF No. 152 is titled "Defendants Meta Platforms, Inc., Accenture LLP,
Genpact Limited, and TaskUs, Inc.'s Consolidated Motion to Dismiss Plaintiff's Second Amended
Complaint Pursuant to Rule 12(b)(6); Memorandum of Points and Authorities." Ex. A at 1.
(C)
Signatories. ECF No. 152 is signed "/s/ Michelle L. Visser" for Orrick, Herrington
& Sutcliffe LLP as "Attorneys for Defendants Meta Platforms, Inc. and Genpact Limited," and is
dated August 13, 2026. Ex. A at 3, 24. It is also signed "/s/ Devin S. Anderson" of Kirkland &
Ellis LLP as "Attorneys for Defendant Accenture LLP" and "/s/ Kristin C. Christensen" of
Ogletree, Deakins, Nash, Smoak & Stewart, P.C. as "Attorneys for Defendants TASKUS, INC."
Ex. A at 25; see also id. at 3 (Anderson signature).
2

(d)
Text of footnote 3. ECF No. 152 contains a footnote numbered 3. It begins on ECF
page 11 of 25 (internal page 3) and ends on ECF page 12 of 25 (internal page 4). Its text reads:
"Beyond the claims raised in this action, Plaintiff has also filed several different actions in
other courts raising baseless claims against some combination of the Defendants. These actions
include: (1) a defamation action against Meta and counsel for Accenture based on arguments in
Accenture's Motion to Dismiss in Plaintiff's original N.D. Cal. Action (Ballentine v. Accenture
LLP, et al., No. 5:26-cv-472 (M.D. Fla.)), which the district court dismissed based on Plaintiff's
'failure to comply with the Standing Order' regarding the disclosure of the use of artificial
intelligence and Plaintiff's 'inability to certify compliance with Rule 11 of the Federal Rules of
Civil Procedure,' Order, Ballentine v. Accenture LLP, et al., No. 5:26-cv-472 (M.D. Fla. July 24,
2026), Dkt. No. 80; (2) a Florida state court action raising both the civil rights claims raised in this
action and Plaintiff's defamation claims (Ballentine v. Meta Platforms, Inc., et al., No. 5:26-cv-213
(M.D. Fla.), removed from No. 35-2026-CA-000494 (Cir. Ct. Lake Cnty.)); and (3) most recently,
a complaint against the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children ('NCMEC') and its
corporate counsel in the Eastern District of Virginia based on allegedly defamatory language in a
letter sent by NCMEC to Plaintiff in response to a subpoena (Ballentine v. Katie Hall, et al., No.
1:26-cv-2331 (E.D. Va.))."
Ex. A at 11-12.
(e)
Reference to this action. Footnote 3 identifies this action by name and case
number: "Ballentine v. Katie Hall, et al., No. 1:26-cv-2331 (E.D. Va.)." Ex. A at 12.
II.
LIMITS OF THE REQUEST
Plaintiff does not request notice that any statement in ECF No. 152 is true.
Plaintiff does not request notice of any purpose, motive, or state of mind of any signatory. Plaintiff
does not request notice that any characterization of this action contained in footnote 3 is accurate.
3

The request is confined to the fact that ECF No. 152 exists, the date it was filed, who signed it,
and what it says.
IV.
RELIEF
6.
Plaintiff requests an order taking judicial notice of the five facts stated in
Paragraph 4. Plaintiff requests that the noticed facts be available for consideration in connection
with ECF Nos. 89, 90, and 93, Plaintiff's motion for leave to amend, and any other matter in which
the Court considers the allegations at ECF No. 59-1 19 164-169 or Proposed Second Am. Compl.
191 180-185. In the alternative, Plaintiff requests an order taking judicial notice of the facts stated
in Paragraph 4(a), (b), (c), and (e). A proposed order accompanies this Request.
Date: November 1, 2026
Respectfully submitted,
Marvelle J. Ballentine
Plaintiff, pro se
1520 Belle View Blvd, Ste. #5847
Alexandria, Virginia 22307
(407) 794-6503
jayballentine@protonmail.com
4

4.
Proposed Order.
Counsel of record for Defendants National Center for Missing & Exploited Children, Katie

Marvelle J. Ballentine
